result.brief:
**Syllabus brief: Processamento de Imagens (CCO074, turma CCONM4B, IESB, 2026/2)**

**General information (p. 1).** The course is taught by Thiago Raposo Milhomem de Carvalho. It is for the 7th period, with 60 h in total (45 theory and 15 practice). The prerequisites are Cálculo II and APC. The ementa covers:
- definitions and fundamentals
- multidimensional Fourier analysis
- enhancement in the spatial and frequency domains
- image filtering and restoration
- color
- transforms
- image coding and compression
- morphology and segmentation

Practical work uses Matlab or Octave (p. 3). Teaching is by lectures with active methodologies, and the Google Classroom virtual learning environment is used (p. 3).

**Units, in order (pp. 1–3)**
1. **Introdução e Fundamentos (p. 1):**
   - principles and applications
   - the human visual system and perception
   - digital image representation
   - acquisition and the mathematical model
   - image parameters
   - pixel relations (adjacency, neighborhood, paths, connectivity)
2. **Operações e Transformações sobre Imagens (pp. 1–2):**
   - logical operations
   - gray-level operations
   - interpolation
   - spatial and geometric operations
   - classification of transformations
   - histograms and equalization
   - spatial masks, convolution and correlation
   - filters
   - Fourier transform
   - sampling and aliasing (including spatial aliasing)
3. **Filtragem no domínio espacial e da frequência: Realce e Restauração (p. 2):**
   - spatial-domain enhancement
   - statistical filters (mean, median, smoothing)
   - sharpening, edge detection, unsharp masking and high-boost
   - frequency-domain filtering: low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and band-reject, using ideal, Butterworth and Gaussian filters
   - homomorphic and notch filters
   - noise and artifacts: characterization and distributions, spectral, spatial, known-source and region-based treatment
   - adaptive filtering
4. **Imagens em Cores (p. 2):**
   - the electromagnetic spectrum and perception
   - additive and subtractive color
   - hue, intensity and saturation
   - RGB, CMY and HSI representations
   - color processing: conversions, quantization, safe colors, slicing
   - equalization, contrast, sharpness and color segmentation
5. **Codificação, Morfologia e Segmentação (pp. 2–3):**
   - compression fundamentals and psycho-visual redundancy
   - information and entropy
   - source and channel coding
   - lossless and lossy compression
   - other transforms: DCT, wavelets, Karhunen-Loève, Walsh-Hadamard
   - main compression techniques
   - image coding and JPEG
   - spatial and temporal redundancy, video coding and MPEG
   - binary images
   - morphological operations on binary images
   - morphology and segmentation of binary images
   - morphology and segmentation in gray levels

The content list has only 5 units. The schedule (p. 7) mentions a "Unidade 6: Morfologia e Segmentação". In the content list, morphology and segmentation sit inside Unit 5.

**Class schedule (classes on Mondays and Tuesdays) (pp. 6–7)**

*1º Bimestre*
- **3 and 4 Aug:** presentation of the plan and the main concepts. Unit 1 and Matlab. (p. 6)
- **10 and 11 Aug:** Units 1 and 2 (Matlab). Possible graded activity. (p. 6)
- **17 and 18 Aug:** Units 1 and 2. Possible graded activity. (p. 6)
- **24 and 25 Aug:** Units 1, 2 and 3. Possible graded activity. (p. 6)
- **31 Aug and 1 Sep:** Units 2 and 3, with review and exercises. (p. 6)
- **7 and 8 Sep:** there is no class on 7 Sep. Units 2 and 3, with review and exercises. (p. 6)
- **14 and 15 Sep: P1.** (p. 6)

*2º Bimestre*
- **21 and 22 Sep:** Units 2 and 3. (p. 6)
- **28 and 29 Sep:** Units 2 and 3. (p. 6)
- **5 and 6 Oct:** Unit 3. (p. 6)
- **12 and 13 Oct:** no classes. (p. 6)
- **19 and 20 Oct:** Units 3, 4 (Cores) and 5 (Codificação). (p. 6)
- **26 and 27 Oct:** Units 3, 4 and 5. (p. 6)
- **2 and 3 Nov:** there is no class on 2 Nov. Units 3, 4 and 5 are covered on 3 Nov. (pp. 6–7)
- **9 and 10 Nov:** Units 3, 4, 5 and 6 (Morfologia e Segmentação), with review and exercises. (p. 7)
- **16 and 17 Nov: P2.** (p. 7)

*After the bimesters*
- **23 and 24 Nov:** all units, with discussion of the exams and clarification of doubts. (p. 7)
- **30 Nov and 1 Dec:** there is no class on 30 Nov. Same content as the previous week. (p. 7)
- **7 and 8 Dec: P3 (substitutive exam)**, followed by closing and delivery of the final reports. (p. 7)

The bimester labels sit in a merged cell in the table, so I read the boundaries from the layout. The 1º Bimestre runs from 3 Aug to P1. The 2º Bimestre runs from 21 Sep to P2 (pp. 6–7).

**P1 vs P2 (exam dates and content)**
- **P1:** it takes place on 14 Sep (Part 1, Monday) and 15 Sep (Part 2, Tuesday). It is written, individual and closed-book. (pp. 4, 6)
- **P2:** it takes place on 16 Nov (Part 1, Monday) and 17 Nov (Part 2, Tuesday). The format is the same. (pp. 4, 7)
- **Content is not stated explicitly for either exam.** From the schedule, the classes before P1 covered Units 1 and 2 and the start of Unit 3 (p. 6). Before P2, the classes covered Units 2 and 3, with Units 4, 5 and 6 added from 19 Oct (pp. 6–7). That is my inference, not something the document says.
- **P3** covers the whole semester's content (p. 4).

**Evaluation criteria (pp. 3–5)**
- All items are graded from 0 to 10.
- **A1 = 0,7·P1 + 0,3·TE1**
- **A2 = 0,7·P2 + 0,3·TE2** (p. 4)
- **TE1 and TE2** are the averages of graded activities other than the written exams. These include exercises, quizzes, tests, labs, simulations, forums and presentations. Each TE is 50% synchronous activities and 50% asynchronous activities, and each half is a simple arithmetic mean. Class participation may count as a graded activity or as extra credit. There are no make-ups for missed graded exercises. (p. 4)
- **MF = 0,4·A1 + 0,6·A2** (p. 4)
- **P3:**
  - It is available if MF < 5,0, and the student must request it.
  - It covers all content and fully replaces A1 or A2, whichever is more favorable.
  - **MF = max{0,4·P3 + 0,6·A2 ; 0,4·A1 + 0,6·P3}** (p. 4)
- **Approval:**
  - A student needs attendance of at least 75% and MF ≥ 5,0.
  - With attendance below 75%, the student fails automatically, has no right to P3, and receives the mention SR. (pp. 4–5)
  - Students on home-exercise regime (exercício domiciliar) must still take the in-person individual exams. (p. 4)
- **Mentions (p. 5):**
  - MF ≥ 9,0: SS (approved)
  - 7,0 to <9,0: MS (approved)
  - 5,0 to <7,0: MM (approved)
  - 3,0 to <5,0: MI (failed)
  - above 0 and <3,0: II (failed)
  - 0,0: SR (failed)
- The plan may be changed during the semester (p. 5).

  - Oppenheim & Schafer, *Discrete-Time Signal Processing*, 2010
  - Gilat, *Matlab com aplicações em engenharia*, 2nd ed., 2006
  - Hanselman, *Matlab 6: Curso Completo*, 2003
  - Phillips, Parr & Riskin, *Signals, Systems, and Transforms*, 4th ed., 2008
